paper.title: Structure-based out-of-distribution (OOD) materials property prediction: a benchmark study
paper.research_summary: This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark study evaluating graph neural networks (GNNs) for predicting materials properties on out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets—materials whose structures or properties deviate significantly from the training distribution. It introduces five OOD test set generation methods (LOCO, SparseXsingle, SparseYsingle, SparseXcluster, SparseYcluster) applied to three MatBench datasets (dielectric, elasticity, perovskites), and benchmarks eight SOTA GNNs, revealing systematic underperformance on OOD tasks compared to i.i.d. baselines and identifying structural and architectural factors underlying robustness differences.

dataset_uses.purpose: Generate OOD test sets via five methods including LOCO, SparseXsingle, SparseYsingle, SparseXcluster, and SparseYcluster.
dataset_uses.construction_method: k-means clustering on OFM features; t-SNE dimensionality reduction; kernel density estimation

evidence.text: Leave-one-cluster-out (LOCO). Meredig et al.45 proposed this approach in their assessment of the generalization performance of ML models for predicting material properties. Initially, we apply the k-means algorithm61 based on the orbital-ﬁeld matrix (OFM) features62 to cluster the whole dataset into 50 clusters.

Single-point targets with the lowest structure density (SparseXsingle). In this method, we begin by converting material structures into the 1024-dimension OFM feature space. Subsequently, we apply the t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE)64 for dimension reduction converting the OFM feature space to a 2D space (x-value). Following this, we calculate the density for each data point in the 2D space and select 500 samples with the lowest density. The density was calculated using Gaussian Kernel Density function of the t-SNE. We apply k-means clustering on these chosen samples to convert them into 50 clusters. Finally, we extract one sample from each cluster, yielding a test set with 50 target samples.
